entries.title: Clayface
entries.review:
Holy shit bro this movie was actually peak. Really loved the whole atmosphere and the story was so good. I really liked how they handled Clayface and everything surrounding his character.
Some scenes were pretty disgusting tho ngl, especially that airplane scene. The whole body horror was actually insane.

The acting, visuals and cinematography were great too. And I really loved the ending. It was sad, but at the same time such a fitting way to end the movie. I think it worked especially well for a DC story. I couldn’t have asked for a better ending.
4.5/5

entries.title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
entries.review:
I actually really like this movie, especially after rewatching it. I remember not enjoying it nearly as much the first time, but honestly I think Solo is massively overhated. The whole atmosphere, visuals and CGI were really great and I also loved the cast. Emilia Clarke, Woody Harrelson and Donald Glover were all great. I know a lot of people didn’t like the recasting of Han Solo, but I honestly didn’t mind it that much. Sure, Alden Ehrenreich isn’t Harrison Ford, but what else were they supposed to do? You can’t make an entire movie with a CGI Han Solo. It works for a few scenes, like Tarkin in Rogue One or Luke in The Mandalorian, but not for a whole movie.

And honestly, after rewatching this and especially with Maul: Shadow Lord, I actually think this movie is more important than people give it credit for. The whole criminal syndicate storyline and Maul’s connection to Qi’ra make it much more interesting now. I’m really curious to see if Season 2 of Shadow Lord will explore that connection further, especially since I’d love to see Qi’ra again.
Of course, the movie isn’t perfect. The way Han gets his last name was pretty stupid and honestly not that well written. But bro that’s such a small thing compared to everything I enjoyed about it. I really don’t understand why some people act like this movie is terrible or completely unnecessary.

4/5

entries.title: Other Mommy
entries.review:
Interesting movie, but tbh I don’t really know what to think about it. I expected something more like Coraline, but somehow it felt like we skipped the entire beginning. Like the movie had just started and it already felt like we were an hour into it.
The CGI didn’t really bother me as much as it apparently bothered other people. But the whole movie just felt kinda weird. We saw the Other Mommy, then everything calmed down, then she showed up again, they drove to another location, she appeared again and then the same thing happened all over again.

What I also found weird was how almost nobody questioned anything. Like when they were at the grandma’s house, sitting by the water in the dark, and nobody even questioned why there were random ball pit balls floating around?
And the ending well, if you’ve seen it, you know what I mean.

I actually liked the monster design though and that one scene where the guy got killed inside the house was genuinely crazy. Like, that was extremely brutal.

Overall, a pretty strange movie with some really good moments, but I don’t think I’d ever rewatch it.

2.5/5

entries.title: Resident Evil
entries.review:
Holy shit, fucking peak cinema bro.
I loved pretty much everything about this movie. Probably one of the best movies of the year for me and definitely the best horror movie of the year. And obviously the best Resident Evil movie ever, but honestly that’s not even close.

I really loved how relatable the main character was. He actually felt like a normal person, missing shots, being clumsy and just reacting like an actual person who isn’t a cop or Jason Statham would. I also really liked how the movie managed to be genuinely funny while still being a horror movie. The monsters looked really fucking good too. But probably the best thing about it was that it actually felt like Resident Evil. Not just some action movie with the Resident Evil name slapped on it. Even little things like the scene with the typewriter were so cool if you know the games.

Spoiler:

I know a lot of people didn’t like the ending, but I honestly thought it was almost perfect. I really couldn’t imagine this movie ending with a happy ending. I maybe would’ve liked him to still get the antidote, but my perfect ending probably would’ve been Raccoon City getting completely destroyed by the bombing right at the end. That would’ve been such a perfect Resident Evil ending.

I really hope we somehow get a second movie. I know the director already said it’s unlikely because of how much hate the movie got from fans, but man, I really hope he gets to do more with this franchise. I’d love to see another one.
